subject: Incident response: notification windows, SCCs, and law-enforcement cooperation
messages:
From: Julia Morales <julia.morales@acme-pharma.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neal Bergman <neal.bergman@bergmanpartners.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on breach notification timelines & cooperation

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Our legal and security teams ran a quick review of the draft DPA and SCCs. Two items popped up that we need explicit confirmation on before we can move to procurement:

1) Notification window: can Redwood commit to a definitive notice window to our security contact when Customer Data is impacted? Our privacy team usually asks for "notice within 72 hours of confirmation" (GDPR-friendly). For HIPAA-regulated data we also need clarity on the maximum notification period.

2) Law enforcement & preservation: if local law enforcement or regulators request preserved logs or expedited access, will Redwood cooperate and, if so, under what process (subpoena, court order, how long will you preserve logs for)?

It would be helpful to see suggested contract language you can accept (brevity preferred). I attached the sections of the SCCs we referenced.

Could you loop in legal/security at Redwood and send back a short answer?

Best,
Julia
Security & Privacy Lead
Acme Pharma

Karthik / Laura — forwarding Acme's ask (see attached). They want clear notification windows and specifics on cooperation with law enforcement / log preservation.

Proposed quick reply (draft):
- We will notify the Customer's designated security contact within 72 hours of confirmation that Customer Data was impacted, and will provide updates as we investigate.
- We will preserve relevant logs for a minimum of 90 days and will cooperate with lawful requests (subpoena/court order).

Laura — can you confirm legal is comfortable with the 72-hour/90-day commitments and suggest precise contract language we should propose? Karthik — FYI for commercial.

Thanks — Hannah

Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification on breach notification timelines & cooperation

Hannah / Karthik — thanks for the draft. A few legal considerations and suggested redlines attached. High level:

- "72 hours of confirmation" is a reasonable commercial commitment, but we should be careful with "confirmation" language. Incident discovery versus confirmation can differ; propose: "within 72 hours of Redwood's confirmation that a security incident has materially affected Customer Data." That gives us necessary operational latitude.

- HIPAA: for covered entity obligations we cannot unilaterally adopt a different statutory timeline. For HIPAA-regulated customers we should reference applicable statutes and offer cooperation; commercial commitment stays the same (72 hours from confirmation) but add phrase "subject to applicable law."

- Law enforcement: we will preserve logs and cooperate with lawful process. We can't commit to voluntary disclosure absent a subpoena or court order. Suggested clause: "Redwood will preserve relevant logs for a minimum of 90 days following identification of an incident and will provide access to such logs to Customer or to law enforcement only in response to a valid legal process, subject to Redwood's obligations to protect other customers and applicable law."

- Evidence requests / additional costs: if Customer requires non-routine collection or long-term forensic services we should reserve the right to bill time & materials.

I attached a DPA breach notice template + a HIPAA SLA redline. Use the DPA template language below in the external reply.

Proposed DPA clause (copyable):
"Breach Notification. In the event Redwood confirms that a security incident has materially affected Customer Data, Redwood will notify Customer's designated security contact without undue delay and, in any case, within seventy-two (72) hours of such confirmation, Redwood will provide an initial notice describing the nature of the incident, affected data categories, and mitigation steps. Redwood will provide timely updates as additional information becomes available. Redwood will preserve relevant logs for a minimum of ninety (90) days and will cooperate with Customer and with law enforcement in accordance with applicable law and valid legal process. Additional investigative assistance beyond Redwood's standard incident response may be provided at Customer's expense."

Let me know if you want me to send the redline directly to Acme with this language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Breach_Notice_Template_v1.docx; HIPAA_SLA_Redline_v2.docx

Subject: Re: Clarification on breach notification timelines & cooperation

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the SCC excerpt. We've reviewed with legal and security and the short answers are below; I've pasted the proposed contract language for your convenience.

Short answers:
- Notification window: Redwood will provide initial notice to Acme's designated security contact within seventy-two (72) hours of Redwood's confirmation that a security incident has materially affected Customer Data. We will provide further updates as the investigation progresses.
- HIPAA: The 72-hour commercial commitment applies; where HIPAA or other law prescribes different statutory obligations, we will comply with applicable law and coordinate on any regulatory filings required of a covered entity.
- Law enforcement & preservation: Redwood will preserve relevant logs for a minimum of ninety (90) days and will cooperate with lawful requests. Redwood will only disclose information to law enforcement in response to valid legal process (e.g., subpoena, court order) unless otherwise required by applicable law.

Proposed clause (for your DPA):
"Breach Notification. In the event Redwood confirms that a security incident has materially affected Customer Data, Redwood will notify Customer's designated security contact without undue delay and, in any case, within seventy-two (72) hours of such confirmation, providing an initial description of the incident, categories of affected data, and mitigation steps. Redwood will provide timely updates as additional information becomes available. Redwood will preserve relevant logs for a minimum of ninety (90) days and will cooperate with Customer and with law enforcement in accordance with applicable law and valid legal process. Additional investigative assistance beyond Redwood's standard incident response may be provided at Customer's expense."

Next steps:
- Laura has attached a redline of the DPA + a HIPAA SLA note (cc'd). Neal — if you want to propose edits, feel free; otherwise we can incorporate this language into the contract redline and share a short summary with procurement.

Would you like us to add the redline to DocuSign now or do you prefer to review first?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
